predecessors.name: Picts
predecessors.text: the Pictish kingdom, from the Forth to the Spey and Fortriu in the tenth century

predecessors.name: Dál Riata
predecessors.text: Argyll, Dal Riata's Cliopatria row, which ends in 899

successors.name: Kingdom of Scotland
successors.text: the whole kingdom, which Cliopatria renames Kingdom of Scotland from 1294

ledger.x: 973: Edgar acknowledges Scottish sovereignty over Lothian.
1099: Cliopatria adds three cells on the western coast (two in Argyll that it draws in the Isles) and drops one in the Highlands.
February 1136: the First Treaty of Durham.
1139: the Second Treaty of Durham gives the earldom of Northumberland to David's son Henry.
1157: Henry II takes back the north.
1234: Galloway comes under the Scottish crown.
1263: the war with Norway for the Hebrides opens at Largs.
2 July 1266: the Treaty of Perth ends the war.
2 July 1266: the Hebrides pass to Scotland.
1286: Alexander III dies and the Alba period ends.
1293: the Alba row ends in Cliopatria and the Kingdom of Scotland row begins in 1294.

wars.name: Brunanburh campaign
wars.outcome: Æthelstan invades Scotland in 934; in 937 Olaf Guthfrithson, Constantine and Owain of Strathclyde invade England and lose at Brunanburh; no frontier changes.

wars.name: Battle of Carham
wars.outcome: Scottish victory over Uhtred of Bamburgh; 'Lothian and the region north of Berwick integrated fully into Scotland' (infobox).

wars.name: David I's invasions of England
wars.outcome: Carlisle and the Northumbrian castles taken January 1136; David keeps Carlisle at the First Treaty of Durham (February 1136); defeat at the Standard (22 August 1138); his son Henry given the earldom of Northumberland by the Second Treaty (1139).

wars.name: Anglo-Scottish claims to the northern counties
wars.outcome: Malcolm IV gives up Cumbria and Northumbria to Henry II in 1157; William the Lion is captured at Alnwick in 1174 (Alba page); on 25 September 1237 the Treaty of York has Alexander II 'quitclaim to the King of England his hereditary rights to the counties of…

wars.name: Scottish-Norwegian war for the Hebrides
wars.outcome: Inconclusive Battle of Largs (1263); the Treaty of Perth (2 July 1266) gives the Hebrides and the Isle of Man to Scotland and leaves Orkney and Shetland to Norway for 4,000 marks and an annuity of 100 marks.

certainty.note: No frontier is dated by treaty or survey on the pages opened.

The Treaty of York (25 September 1237) 'officially defined' the Anglo-Scottish border 'for the first time and by mutual agreement'; the Treaty of Perth (2 July 1266) fixes the Norwegian frontier at Orkney and Shetland.
